stories.headline: Trump administration asks OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6 release, vetting customers one by one

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration asked OpenAI to limit the release of GPT-5.6 to only a small set of government-approved partners before any wider release, citing security concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration has asked OpenAI to limit the release of its next model, GPT-5.6, to only a small set of government-approved partners before any wider release, citing security concerns, according to a source familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman told employees Wednesday in a company Q&A that GPT-5.6 would launch in limited preview to a small group of enterprise customers, with the government approving access customer by customer during the preview period.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman told employees Wednesday in a company Q&A that it would release GPT-5.6 in limited preview form... During that preview period, the Trump administration itself would reportedly approve access for customers on a case-by-case basis.

key_facts.fact: The request for a staggered release came from conversations with the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy.
key_facts.excerpt: The request for a staggered release came from conversations with two key government agencies, the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

key_facts.fact: Altman discussed GPT-5.6 with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday; a source said the government intervened because the model has 'Mythos-like' capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman discussed GPT-5.6 with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday... The source said the government intervened because GPT-5.6 has 'Mythos-like' capability.

key_facts.fact: Altman said in the memo this is 'not our preferred long term model' and that he hopes to release GPT-5.6 more broadly a 'couple of weeks later'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We've made clear to the US government that this is not our preferred long term model"... hopefully followed a "couple of weeks later" by a more general release of the 5.6 model.

key_facts.fact: The move follows an AI security executive order Trump signed earlier this month directing agencies to stand up a voluntary testing protocol for AI companies before releasing new models.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump signed an executive order earlier this month asking AI companies to participate in a voluntary federal review of their more powerful models before they are publicly released.

stories.headline: OpenAI leans toward delaying IPO to 2027 as Altman holds firm on $1T valuation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is leaning toward holding off its IPO until 2027, according to the New York Times citing three people involved in the company's deliberations.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is leaning towards holding off on an initial public offering until 2027, the New York Times reported, citing three people involved in the company's deliberations.

key_facts.fact: The company had hired bankers and lawyers eyeing an IPO as soon as the third or fourth quarter of this year, with Altman pushing advisers to find a way to value OpenAI at $1 trillion, up from its last private valuation of $730 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The maker of ChatGPT hired bankers and lawyers with an eye toward a public offering as soon as the third or fourth quarter of this year... Sam Altman... pushed those advisers to find a way for the start-up to be valued at $1 trillion, up from the company's last private valuation of $730 billion.

key_facts.fact: Advisers presented executives with two options — wait until 2027 to go public at $1 trillion, or lower the valuation for a quicker IPO — and Altman called any change to the trillion-dollar valuation a 'nonstarter'.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's advisers presented company executives with the option of waiting until 2027 to go public with a $1 trillion valuation, or lower the targeted valuation for a quicker I.P.O. Mr. Altman... responded that any change to the trillion-dollar valuation was a nonstarter.

key_facts.fact: Bankers cautioned that recent volatility in tech stocks and in SpaceX's shares after its record IPO could dampen retail-investor enthusiasm for an OpenAI offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Bankers advising the ChatGPT maker on its IPO plans cautioned that recent volatility in tech stocks, as well as in SpaceX's shares following its record IPO, could dampen enthusiasm from retail investors for OpenAI's offering.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI filed confidentially for an IPO with the SEC, disclosing the move in a June 9 statement that said it had not decided on timing.
key_facts.excerpt: The company filed confidentially for an IPO with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, according to a statement on June 9. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while..."

stories.headline: General Intuition raises $320M at $2.3B led by Khosla to train AI agents on gameplay

key_facts.fact: General Intuition said it raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation, bringing total disclosed funding to $454 million after the $134 million round it raised at launch last October.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, General Intuition said it raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation... The round brings General Intuition's total disclosed funding to $454 million, after the $134 million round it raised at launch last October.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Nico Rosberg, and researchers at Google DeepMind and MIT.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition's latest round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Nico Rosberg, and researchers at Google DeepMind and MIT.

key_facts.fact: The startup spun out of Medal, a platform for uploading and sharing video game clips; the hundreds of millions of hours of uploaded gameplay provided the initial dataset to train its models.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup was spun out of de Witte's other company, Medal... The hundreds of millions of hours of uploaded gameplay provided the initial dataset to train General Intuition.

key_facts.fact: General Intuition describes itself as a frontier AI lab building large action foundation models and world models to train agents that can act across space and time, including physical robots.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition describes itself as a frontier AI lab focused on developing systems that can act across space and time... building large action foundation models trained on billions of action-labeled gameplay clips collected through Medal.

key_facts.fact: Khosla called large action models 'the next big leap', and CEO Pim de Witte said the funding will partly buy GPUs to build a new class of frontier models for agents and robots.
key_facts.excerpt: "Large action models are the next big leap..." said Vinod Khosla... De Witte said the company is raising the funding in part to acquire graphics processing units (GPUs)... to build a new class of frontier models which enable agents or physical robots to perceive, predict, and act in any environment.

stories.headline: Patronus AI raises $50M Series B and unveils Digital World Models to stress-test AI agents

key_facts.fact: Patronus AI announced a $50 million Series B led by Greenfield Partners, bringing the company's total funding to $70 million.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, the company announced a $50 million Series B round led by Greenfield Partners, with participation from Notable Capital, Lightspeed, Datadog, and Samsung. The round brings the company's total funding to $70 million.

key_facts.fact: Patronus AI was founded in 2023 by former Meta AI researchers Anand Kannappan and Rebecca Qian, and its revenue has grown more than 15-fold over the past year.
key_facts.excerpt: Patronus AI, a startup founded in 2023 by former Meta AI researchers Anand Kannappan and Rebecca Qian... Patronus' revenue has grown 15-fold over the past year, fueling significant investor interest.

key_facts.fact: The company unveiled Digital World Models — language diffusion world models that create replicas of websites and enterprise systems where agents are stress-tested after reinforcement-learning training.
key_facts.excerpt: Patronus AI... unveiled its Digital World Models, a new class of large-scale simulation environments designed to help AI systems train, evaluate, and improve across complex digital workflows... language diffusion world models that are designed to scale the creation of simulation data to train and evaluate AI agent actions.

key_facts.fact: Patronus says it works with the majority of the world's leading frontier AI labs and hyperscalers, and will use the capital to expand research, engineering, and compute.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Patronus AI works with the majority of the world's leading frontier AI labs and hyperscalers.

stories.headline: California launches first-in-nation AI job-loss tracker tying jobless claims to AI exposure

key_facts.fact: California introduced a first-in-the-nation online tracking tool, the California AI-Unemployment Tracker, to monitor and detect AI-related job loss as an early warning system.
key_facts.excerpt: California today introduced a first-in-the-nation online tracking tool to monitor and detect AI-related job loss... an early warning system to help the state monitor, track, and anticipate job loss.

key_facts.fact: The dashboard links unemployment insurance claims with measures of occupational AI exposure and was developed in partnership with the California Policy Lab at UCLA and the Employment Development Department, as part of a May executive order by Gov. Newsom.
key_facts.excerpt: The California AI-Unemployment Tracker links unemployment insurance claims with measures of occupational AI exposure... Developed through a partnership with Gov. Gavin Newsom's office, the California Employment Development Department and the nonpartisan California Policy Lab.

key_facts.fact: A report found no evidence as of May 2026 of a statewide surge in layoffs in highly AI-exposed occupations, but unemployment claims rose among college-educated workers in high-AI-exposure occupations and among such workers in the San Francisco Bay Area.
key_facts.excerpt: A report... finds no evidence as of May 2026 of a statewide surge in layoffs among workers in highly AI-exposed occupations. However... Unemployment insurance claims rose among college-educated workers in occupations with high exposure to AI, as well as those in occupations with high AI exposure in the San Francisco Bay area.

key_facts.fact: The tracker will be updated monthly and breaks claims down by region, industry, age, education, race, ethnicity and gender; it follows more than 121,000 tech layoffs this year.
key_facts.excerpt: With planned monthly updates, it breaks down claims by region, industry, age, education, race, ethnicity and gender... According to tech layoff tracker Layoffs.fyi, more than 121,000 tech employees have been laid off this year.

stories.headline: Warp raises $60M Series B led by Battery to automate payroll and HR with AI agents

key_facts.fact: Warp raised a $60 million Series B led by Battery Ventures, bringing its total funding to $85 million in under a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing a $60 million Series B led by Battery Ventures, with participation from Peak XV, Sound Ventures, and Y Combinator. It brings our total funding to $85 million in just under a year.

key_facts.fact: The round drew participation from Peak XV, Sound Ventures and Y Combinator plus operators including Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke, former Stripe COO Claire Hughes Johnson, Dropbox's co-founders and Balaji Srinivasan.
key_facts.excerpt: Battery Ventures led the Series B round. Peak XV, Sound Ventures, Y Combinator and HOF Capital also took part, along with a list of founders and operators that included Shopify Inc. Chief Executive Tobias Lütke, former Stripe Inc. operating chief Claire Hughes Johnson, Dropbox Inc. co-founders Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi... Balaji Srinivasan.

key_facts.fact: The New York-based startup pitches itself as an AI-native alternative to Workday-style HR software, with agents that run payroll in seconds across all 50 states, file multi-state returns and clear tax notices without a person in the loop.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York-based company pitches itself as an AI-native alternative to legacy human capital management software, the category long dominated by Workday... Payroll runs in seconds across all 50 states and its software agents file returns and clear the tax notices that follow without a person in the loop.

key_facts.fact: Warp doubled its annual recurring revenue in Q1, is on track to process over $2 billion in annual payroll volume, and plans to grow its New York workforce from 50 to 200 over the next year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has expanded its total funding to $85m in less than a year, doubled its annualized recurring revenue (ARR) in Q1, and is on track to process over $2 billion in total annual payroll volume... intends to use the funds to... scale its in-person workforce in New York from 50 to 200 employees over the next year.

stories.headline: Meta Superintelligence Labs hires three Virtue AI founders to boost AI security

key_facts.fact: Meta Superintelligence Labs is hiring three Virtue AI co-founders — Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo — along with other members of the AI security startup's team.
key_facts.excerpt: Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo, leaders in AI security, are joining Meta Superintelligence Labs, according to an internal post viewed by Axios.

key_facts.fact: Li and Song will report to Meta Superintelligence Labs executive Nat Friedman, while Koyejo will report to Rob Fergus, head of Meta's fundamental AI research lab FAIR; the terms were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Li and Song will report into Nat Friedman, a Meta Superintelligence Lab executive. Sanmi Koyejo will report into Rob Fergus, head of FAIR, Meta's fundamental AI research lab... The terms of the arrangement were not disclosed.

key_facts.fact: Virtue AI develops enterprise AI security tools spanning automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance.
key_facts.excerpt: The hires also include members of Virtue AI's broader team, which develops enterprise AI security tools spanning automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance.

key_facts.fact: The arrangement is a hiring of founders and some team members rather than a clean acquisition of the company, its IP or its full workforce.
key_facts.excerpt: Axios described a hiring arrangement involving three founders and other Virtue AI team members, not a purchase of the company, its IP, its contracts or the whole workforce.

key_facts.fact: An internal memo framed the rationale by saying keeping AI systems safe, reliable and trustworthy is 'foundational' as Meta ships AI products to billions of people.
key_facts.excerpt: An internal memo framed the rationale plainly: "As we ship AI products to billions of people and build increasingly capable agents, keeping those systems safe, reliable, and trustworthy is foundational."
